content.comment_body: Hello, I'm sorry for this beginner-level question, but I haven't been able to find an answer anywhere. I want to create a tracker that records how long Q1 is ON, so I can replace it when necessary. I need it to keep tracking the time even if Q1 turns OFF and then ON again. Are there any resources you recommend? Thank you very much and have a wonderful Sunday!
You should use the Stopwatch function.

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your response! I realized that the stopwatch is probably the best way to count this time, but I'm unsure how to save its value in case of a power loss. Is the stopwatch value always retained in non-volatile memory, or is it stored in RAM?
It may help if you clarify your exact needs. Are you trying to record the ON times for something like a motor, or do you want to switch to a different motor after a specific runtime?

I need to build a counter that warns me at a set runtime (currently 8000 hours) to replace lamps. Since that's a long period, I need the data to survive power outages. Ideally, I would have two triggers: one notification at 6000 hours and another at 8000 hours. I don't need to track down to the exact second—maybe it's possible to have it increment every 10 minutes? I'm just learning about what's possible.

In that case, I recommend using two hour counters (available as pre-made blocks in [product_name]). These counters store running hours in non-volatile memory. The counter increments every complete minute. You can set a target runtime that activates an output and triggers a notification.

Thank you, [user_name], for your assistance! Your help was invaluable! Here is the schematic I created—does it look correct? I want to operate everything using a single button: if held down, it resets the timers; the 6000-hour timer triggers a flashing light, while the 8000-hour timer activates a permanent light.

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are exploring ways to build a time-on tracker for an output, which requires non-volatile storage of runtime hours. The main challenge is ensuring the tracked time persists through power outages and setting up notifications at specific milestones. There is some uncertainty regarding how memory operates for counters and how to access suitable function blocks in logic programming for this application.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for a straightforward method to log and retain ON time for an output, with reliable data preservation after power loss and notifications at configurable time intervals, all with minimal setup complexity.
